programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: The bats that nest in Grandad's shed each year are missing. Can Stan and Gran encourage these nocturnal creatures to return when they can't hear them? Tha na h-ialtagan a tha a' neadachadh ann an sead' an t-Seanair gach bliadhn', air a dhol a dhìth. An tèid aig Dan is Gran air na creutairean oidhcheach seo a thàladh air ais nuair nach cluinnear 'ad?

programme.title: Beathaichean a’ Bocadaich
programme.desc: Tha Sophie a’ coimhead tron phrosbaig sheunta aice airson faicinn ciamar a bhios beathaichean a’ bocadaich. Tha i ag ionnsachadh mar a bhios diofar bheathaichean a’ gluasad agus cuide ri a caraidean, tha i a’ cruthachadh dannsa. An-diugh, danns coltach ri muncaidh agus ròn! Sophie looks through her magic binoculars to find out how animals boogie. She learns how different animals dance and, along with her friends, creates a dance using animal movements. Join her and dance like a monkey and a seal!

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Tha Sif, Pipp agus Bran a’ cleachdadh foidhle gus long-fhànais a chruthachadh. Ziff, Pipp and Button use kitchen foil to create and launch an out-of-this-world spaceship.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha a’ Chearc Iarrainn ’son dannsa còmhla ri na Clangairean ach cho do thuig i gun robh dannsa cho doirbh! Saoil an dèan i chùis air? The Iron Chicken wants to dance with the Clangers, but she didn’t realise dancing was so difficult! Will she manage it?

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Nuair tha na Clangairean air planaid annasach ùr a lorg, tha ’ad 'son dèanamh beagan rannsachaidh. An dèidh dhaibh a dhol air chall, tha 'ad fortanach g' eil Granaidh faisg air làimh 'son an sàbhaladh. When the Clangers find a fascinating new planet, they do a little exploring. When they go astray, it’s lucky that Granny is nearby to save them.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Joy Dunlop a’ leughadh Finn is na Breugan Beaga. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh is a dhealbhachadh le Hugh Percival agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Màiri NicCumhais. A bedtime story for young children. Joy Dunlop reads Finn is na Breugan Beaga, written and illustrated by Hugh Percival and translated into Gaelic by Mairi MacCuish.

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Tha Hanka aona bhliadhna-deug, à Slobhagia, ‘s bidh i a' dol don aon sgoil san t-saoghal a tha a’ teagasg seabhagaireachd mar phàirt den churraicealam àbhaisteach. Hanka is 11, from Slovakia, and she attends the only school in the world where falconry is taught as part of the regular curriculum.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Chan eil Belle, Sebastian is Adele ‘son Là a’ Bhìobhair a chall, ach ciamar a gheibh iad air sin a dhèanamh gun fhiosta do dh'Elaina – gu h-àraidh seach gu bheil Sonaidh air an leantainn? Belle, Sebastian and Adele don’t want to miss Groundhog Day, but how can they do this without Elaina noticing, especially since Sonny has followed them?

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha an taigh ri sgeadachadh ach tha Bitzer feumach air taic nuair tha e air fhàgail os cionn ghnothaichean. Ach 's e barrachd bacadh tha e a' faighinn bhon threud seach cuideachadh - abair bùrach! When the farmer pops out for more supplies, Bitzer is left in charge of decorating and calls on the flock for help. He soon realises this may be a terrible mistake, as they have their own way of doing things - painting and decorating isn't their strong point!

programme.title: Uaine
programme.desc: Tha pailteas de stòras nàdarra an Alba agus tha Calum a’ tadhal air trì pròiseactan eadar-dhealaichte airson sùil a ghabhail air an seòrsa cumhachd a dh’fhaodadh sinn a bhith a’ cruthachadh san àm ri teachd. Scotland is a country full of untapped natural resources and Calum visits three different projects to find out about the kind of energy we could be producing in the future.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Tha sinn air ais ann an Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche airson teirm ùr. Tha tòrr air tachairt thairis air na saor-làithean. Cha robh an là in-sheirbheis cho soirbheachail `s a bha Maighstir Mackle an dùil agus tha Ms Sharpe air nochdadh sna pàipearan-naidheachd ri linn ‘s na thachair aig a’ Mhòd. Our cameras are back at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche for a new term. A lot has happened over the holidays. The in-service day wasn’t as successful as Mr Mackle had hoped and Ms Sharpe has made the newspapers after what happened at the Mòd.

programme.title: Dùbhlain DIY (Instructions Not Included)
programme.desc: With two couples left, Derek 'Pluto' Murray hosts the final of this knockout amateur DIY competition. Derek 'Pluto' Moireach le farpais spòrsail DIY is cupail a’ strì an aghaidh a chèile.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Orchestral musician Liam Lynch from Dunfermline chats to Joy, while Calum researches a traditional event which often precedes a wedding in many parts of rural Scotland.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Sona
programme.desc: Tha Vicky Kilgour, le cuid meas air sauna, a’ gabhail a’ rathaid air costa an iar na h-Alba agus i a’ sireadh sunnd is toileachas, le a caraid Donnchadh Dòmhnallach na cuideachd. Bidh dreach air leth saorsnail air an eapasod seo, agus an dithis aca a’ feuchainn a-mach beagan yòga agus a’ gabhail tlachd ann an seisean dian de shearapaidh-fuaim. Às a sin, togaidh iad orra gu uaigneas draoidheil Chnòideart, agus Tuathanas Coimhearsnachd na sgìre, far an cuir iad an sgilean gu feum ann am gàrradh-margaidh. Sauna lover Vicky Kilgour embarks on a road trip up Scotland’s west coast in search of well-being and happiness, with friend Duncan MacDonald along for the ride. The pair try out some yoga and enjoy an intensive sound therapy session, before heading off to the magically remote world of Knoydart Community Farm where they dabble in some market gardening. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: An Lot/The Croft
programme.desc: Donald Macsween, or 'Sweeny', as he is best known, is back with the latest news from his croft in Ness.

programme.title: Transatlantic Sessions
programme.desc: Featuring musical stars Mike McGoldrick, Aly Bain, Jerry Douglas, Aoife O’ Donovan and Mary Chapin Carpenter.

programme.title: Na Sgiobairean mu Dheireadh/The Last Captains
programme.desc: Series that follows determined fishermen across the fishing seasons

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc: Katie MacRitchie from Harris joins Angus Mackay to go fishing on a moody, misty summer's morning off the east coast of Lewis. Watched closely by a golden eagle, they fish for mackerel as the sun gradually emerges and chat about the role that fishing plays in the community life of the islands. Tha Katie NicRisnidh às na Hearadh còmhla ri Aonghas MacAoidh agus iad ag iasgach air madainn shamhraidh ghruamach, cheòthach far costa an ear Leòdhais. Tha iad ag iasgach airson rionnach, le iolaire-bhuidhe gan coimhead, fhad ’s a nochdas a’ ghrian mean air mhean agus iad a’ bruidhinn mun àite a th’ aig iasgach ann am beatha coimhearsnachd nan h-eileanan.

programme.title: Port
programme.desc: Music documentary in which Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh explore shared musical roots in Donegal.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Beginning at London Marylebone, the last great Victorian railway terminus to be built in the capital, Michael Portillo embarks on a postwar exploration of Britain’s southern counties. He travels to Denham in Buckinghamshire, where engineers are constructing a striking new viaduct, High Wycombe, a historic centre of furniture-making thanks to its abundant of beechwood forest, and Oxford, where he discovers the postwar origins of the charity shop. In the Wiltshire countryside, Michael meets the head of the Soil Association and some of her saddleback piglets to hear how the organic movement was founded after the Second World War in reaction to the intensification of farming.

programme.title: The American Revolution
programme.desc: The British Army under General Cornwallis struggles to pacify the southern states. Meanwhile, one of the most respected American generals betrays the cause and defects to the British. Supported by the French Army and Navy, Washington’s Continental Army wins the decisive victory at Yorktown. Peace is restored, independence is won, and Americans aspire for a more perfect union. A film by Ken Burns, Sarah Botstein and David Schmidt

programme.title: This World
programme.desc: Adventurer and journalist Simon Reeve heads to east Africa to uncover the stories behind the nation's favourite drink. While we drink millions of cups of the stuff each day, how many of us know where our tea actually comes from? The surprising answer is that most of the leaves that go into our everyday teabags do not come from India or China but are bought from an auction in the coastal city of Mombasa in Kenya. From here, Simon follows the tea trail through the epic landscapes of Kenya and Uganda and meets some of the millions of people who pick, pack and transport our tea. Drinking tea with everyone from Masai cattle herders to the descendants of the original white tea planters, Simon learns that the industry that supplies our everyday cuppa is not immune to the troubles of the continent - poverty, low wages and child labour.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo joins Navy Wings pilots for a spectacular close formation flight in the skies over Royal Naval Air Station Yeovilton. He also visits the magnificent Elizabethan mansion of Longleat, seat of the Marquesses of Bath, to find out about the estate’s remarkable survival after the Second World War. At Chippenham in Wiltshire, Michael pays a call on a signalling manufacturer that has been at the heart of British railway projects for decades and has a go on the centre’s simulator, driving the Elizabeth Line train to Paddington.

programme.title: Canal Boat Diaries
programme.desc: Narrowboater Robbie Cumming begins his 170-mile journey across the north of England and soon runs into difficulty when he encounters a problem with his craft's propeller in Wigan and runs aground in Blackburn. Nevertheless, he pushes on to navigate a true wonder of the waterways, the Burnley Embankment.

programme.title: Universe
programme.desc: It’s the ultimate question: why are we here? Brian Cox explores how cutting-edge space missions take us back 13.8 billion years to the origin of the universe.

programme.title: The Nazis: A Warning from History
programme.desc: 'We used to shoot them, give them up as lost, and that was it.' - Petras Zelionka, former member of the Nazi killing squad. How could it happen? How was it possible that the Nazis created killing factories in order to exterminate the Jews and others they thought 'undesirable'? Filmed in Poland, Germany and Lithuania, this documentary demonstrates how the invasion of the Soviet Union in June 1941, in the fulfilment of Hitler's ideological vision, was a crucial catalyst to the radicalisation of the Nazi policy against the Jews. With the help of archive discoveries and frank interviews with victims, bystanders and a former member of a Nazi killing squad, The Road to Treblinka traces the decision-making process that led to one of the greatest crimes the world has ever seen - the Holocaust.

programme.title: Afoot Again in the Past
programme.desc: Simon Thurley investigates the forgotten tunnels of Henry VIII's sewage system at Hampton Court.

programme.title: Our Friends in the North
programme.desc: As a new decade approaches, the friends are divided again. Nicky stands for Parliament, Tosker falls in love with the woman of his dreams and Geordie begins to deal in drugs.

programme.title: Our Friends in the North

programme.title: Bikes!
programme.desc: County Armagh's Tandragee 100 is an event with plenty of history and plenty of challenge. Its 5.3 mile layout is fast and technical, with its fair share of jumps, elevation changes and fast straights which attracts top riders and thousands of spectators. Always a spectacle, the Tandragee 100 has seen notable wins from Guy Martin, Joey Dunlop, Ryan Farquhar, Philip McCallen and, most recently, Michael Dunlop. Stephen Watson presents coverage of the 2026 Tandragee 100.

programme.title: In Ten Pictures
programme.desc: Britney Spears was one of the biggest pop stars of her generation. She grew up in the limelight, and like so many music stars, she was defined by imagery. But she was also the subject of extraordinary exploitation and control. Years of personal and professional turmoil would play out in the frenzied glare of the media spotlight: breakups, breakdowns and familial fall outs. From the over-sexualisation of a child performer to the very public struggles with her mental health, this is the story of a manufactured child star fighting for control over her music, her life and her image.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: We see the culmination of an epic, six-and-a-half-year project in the West Midlands. Martel loves showing off properties in Scotland. The one she visits in Livingston may not be the finest example but it has potential. Dion is impressed by the space on offer in Leeds.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Imagine a warehouse bigger than a football pitch, full of some of science’s most important items. Near Swindon, Christina Trevanion visits the Science and Innovation Park to see some of the 400,000 objects stored there on behalf of England’s science museums. Among the most treasured items are personal possessions from the office of the late Professor Stephen Hawking, including a wheelchair, his specially adapted glasses and a figurine of his Simpsons character. Hoping for a breakthrough of their own are two teams of friends and colleagues browsing a bustling antiques fair in Exeter. In red are Vickie and Hannah, activities coordinators at the same care home, who watch the show every day with their residents! In blue are palliative care nurses Lindsay and Sarah, who both admit to being mad about dogs. With expert Ben Cooper in tow, the reds steer a course for a ship’s wheel, but Captain Cooper isn’t impressed with the high price. The blues alongside Gary Pe are true to their word, sidetracked by an art-deco-style dog statue and then distracted by the real thing in the arms of its owner!

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael arrives in the home of Japanese porcelain, Arita, where a railway line runs straight through the town’s stunning ceramic Shinto shrine. He learns about the traditional blue underglaze, gosu, and turns his hand to pottery decoration. Japan’s volcanic geology means the country is full of thermal spa resorts. Michael stays in a ryokan, a traditional hotel with paper walls and tatami mats where he enjoys a relaxing soak in an onsen, a natural thermal bath. Michael ends this leg in Fukuoka, Japan’s fast-growing city, full of young Japanese who flock there for the food culture and entrepreneurial spirit. At one of the many street food stalls, Michael meets the mayor, an ex-TV presenter turned politician who is transforming the city.

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway tour through Uzbekistan continues in the lush oasis surrounding the historic city of Samarkand. Here, he uncovers the Central Asian origins of the apple, a fruit that travelled to Europe along the Silk Road. Exploring vast orchards, he witnesses how millions of apples are grown and processed here each year. Boarding a high-speed train along the old Trans-Caspian Railway, Michael hears how the Russians toiled to build this remarkable line through the shifting sands of Uzbekistan’s steppe. In Bukhara, he explores the faded magnificence of an abandoned Russian imperial palace. He then enters the city’s Islamic heart, and standing in the shadow of the Ark, the city's striking fortified citadel, he unearths the deadly intrigue between Britain and Russia in what became known as the Great Game - and discovers the fate of two British officers thrown into the infamous 'bug pit'.

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: On a visit to the Kent coast, Ben Robinson learns how an exclusive retreat for the rich and famous suddenly became 'Hellfire Corner' during World War II. Ben examines graffiti in an exclusive visit to a secret air raid shelter and tours the site of Britain’s biggest guns. On the beach, the archaeologist runs his eye over the secret hideaway where Noel Coward and his partner lived after the war.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Priya finds herself trapped. Jack pushes Kim to visit Denise. Kojo asks Harry and Gina to help him find a girlfriend.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: Painting conservator Lucia tackles a crumbling 175-year-old portrait that’s been cut in two, and a pair of baby shoes holding precious memories of wartime heroism are restored.

programme.title: Greece with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: In the first episode of this two-part travel series, Simon Reeve travels from the islands of the Aegean to Greece's capital, Athens. To learn more about Greece and the Greeks, he meets an extraordinary cast of characters, from gun-toting priests to the last remaining sponge divers. Getting behind the picture postcard image of this beautiful country, he finds out how the Greeks are coming to terms with a seemingly endless crisis.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: It’s been more than 15 years since Gareth and Tim from The Office – aka Mackenzie Crook and Martin Freeman – last laid eyes on each other, but the groundbreaking comedy's 25th anniversary has brought them together once again. They share their memories of working, and laughing, alongside Ricky Gervais, co-writer Stephen Merchant and their other leading office colleague Lucy Davis, who played the object of Tim's affections, Dawn. Amongst the anecdotes are the tale of how Martin initially auditioned to play Gareth, how Mackenzie embraced one of TV's worst-ever haircuts, how Ricky came close to ruining filming on a daily basis, and what it was like to be at the heart of 'Office-mania' when the show was at its peak. On top of all that, we get Mackenzie and Martin's views on the American version of the show and find out some of their personal favourite Wernham Hogg moments.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: Wimbledon
programme.desc: A look back at the day’s play at Wimbledon.

programme.title: My Summer of Love
programme.desc: Drama from acclaimed director Pawel Pawlikowski (Last Resort). In the Yorkshire countryside, working-class tomboy Mona meets the exotic, pampered Tamsin. Over the summer season, the two young women discover they have much to teach one another and much to explore together. Mona, behind a spiky exterior, hides an untapped intelligence and a yearning for something beyond the emptiness of her daily life. Tamsin is well-educated, spoiled and cynical. Complete opposites, each is wary of the other's differences when they first meet, but this coolness soon melts into mutual fascination, amusement and attraction. Adding volatility is Mona's older brother Phil, who has renounced his criminal past for religious fervor - which he tries to impose upon his sister. Mona, however, is experiencing her own rapture. 'We must never be parted', Tamsin intones to Mona.

Boarding a high-speed train along the old Trans-Caspian Railway, Michael hears how the Russians toiled to build this remarkable line through the shifting sands of Uzbekistan’s steppe. In Bukhara, he explores the faded magnificence of an abandoned Russian imperial palace. He then enters the city’s Islamic heart, and standing in the shadow of the Ark, the city's striking fortified citadel, he unearths the deadly intrigue between Britain and Russia in what became known as the Great Game - and discovers the fate of two British officers thrown into the infamous 'bug pit'.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: It’s been more than 15 years since Gareth and Tim from The Office – aka Mackenzie Crook and Martin Freeman – last laid eyes on each other, but the groundbreaking comedy's 25th anniversary has brought them together once again. They share their memories of working, and laughing, alongside Ricky Gervais, co-writer Stephen Merchant and their other leading office colleague Lucy Davis, who played the object of Tim's affections, Dawn. Amongst the anecdotes are the tale of how Martin initially auditioned to play Gareth, how Mackenzie embraced one of TV's worst-ever haircuts, how Ricky came close to ruining filming on a daily basis, and what it was like to be at the heart of 'Office-mania' when the show was at its peak. On top of all that, we get Mackenzie and Martin's views on the American version of the show and find out some of their personal favourite Wernham Hogg moments.

programme.title: My Summer of Love
programme.desc: Drama from acclaimed director Pawel Pawlikowski (Last Resort). In the Yorkshire countryside, working-class tomboy Mona meets the exotic, pampered Tamsin. Over the summer season, the two young women discover they have much to teach one another and much to explore together. Mona, behind a spiky exterior, hides an untapped intelligence and a yearning for something beyond the emptiness of her daily life. Tamsin is well-educated, spoiled and cynical. Complete opposites, each is wary of the other's differences when they first meet, but this coolness soon melts into mutual fascination, amusement and attraction. Adding volatility is Mona's older brother Phil, who has renounced his criminal past for religious fervor - which he tries to impose upon his sister. Mona, however, is experiencing her own rapture. 'We must never be parted', Tamsin intones to Mona.

programme.title: Springwatch

programme.title: In Ten Pictures
programme.desc: Britney Spears was one of the biggest pop stars of her generation. She grew up in the limelight, and like so many music stars, she was defined by imagery. But she was also the subject of extraordinary exploitation and control. Years of personal and professional turmoil would play out in the frenzied glare of the media spotlight: breakups, breakdowns and familial fall outs. From the over-sexualisation of a child performer to the very public struggles with her mental health, this is the story of a manufactured child star fighting for control over her music, her life and her image.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: We see the culmination of an epic, six-and-a-half-year project in the West Midlands. Martel loves showing off properties in Scotland. The one she visits in Livingston may not be the finest example but it has potential. Dion is impressed by the space on offer in Leeds.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Imagine a warehouse bigger than a football pitch, full of some of science’s most important items. Near Swindon, Christina Trevanion visits the Science and Innovation Park to see some of the 400,000 objects stored there on behalf of England’s science museums. Among the most treasured items are personal possessions from the office of the late Professor Stephen Hawking, including a wheelchair, his specially adapted glasses and a figurine of his Simpsons character. Hoping for a breakthrough of their own are two teams of friends and colleagues browsing a bustling antiques fair in Exeter. In red are Vickie and Hannah, activities coordinators at the same care home, who watch the show every day with their residents! In blue are palliative care nurses Lindsay and Sarah, who both admit to being mad about dogs. With expert Ben Cooper in tow, the reds steer a course for a ship’s wheel, but Captain Cooper isn’t impressed with the high price. The blues alongside Gary Pe are true to their word, sidetracked by an art-deco-style dog statue and then distracted by the real thing in the arms of its owner!

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael arrives in the home of Japanese porcelain, Arita, where a railway line runs straight through the town’s stunning ceramic Shinto shrine. He learns about the traditional blue underglaze, gosu, and turns his hand to pottery decoration. Japan’s volcanic geology means the country is full of thermal spa resorts. Michael stays in a ryokan, a traditional hotel with paper walls and tatami mats where he enjoys a relaxing soak in an onsen, a natural thermal bath. Michael ends this leg in Fukuoka, Japan’s fast-growing city, full of young Japanese who flock there for the food culture and entrepreneurial spirit. At one of the many street food stalls, Michael meets the mayor, an ex-TV presenter turned politician who is transforming the city.

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway tour through Uzbekistan continues in the lush oasis surrounding the historic city of Samarkand. Here, he uncovers the Central Asian origins of the apple, a fruit that travelled to Europe along the Silk Road. Exploring vast orchards, he witnesses how millions of apples are grown and processed here each year. In Bukhara, he explores the faded magnificence of an abandoned Russian imperial palace. He then enters the city’s Islamic heart, and standing in the shadow of the Ark, the city's striking fortified citadel, he unearths the deadly intrigue between Britain and Russia in what became known as the Great Game - and discovers the fate of two British officers thrown into the infamous 'bug pit'.

programme.title: Shark Bites
programme.desc: Steve Backshall meets the most colossal shark in our seas. Measuring up to a record 18 metres, the whale shark is not only the largest shark, but the largest fish in the world. Steve dives with this gargantuan shark off the coast of Mozambique in Africa and reveals their somewhat surprising diet, before heading into his shark lab to get under their skin and reveal how they manage to filter their food from the water.

programme.title: Jamie Johnson FC
programme.desc: It’s all change at Hawx Academy as former Foxborough player Charlie must prove herself to her teammates, their new coach and an all-access documentary crew.

programme.title: Jamie Johnson FC

programme.title: Shaun the Sheep

programme.title: Dennis & Gnasher Unleashed!
programme.desc: The kids of Beanotown decide that they can run the town far better than the grown-ups. However, they discover it isn’t nearly as easy or fun as they had hoped.

programme.title: Dennis & Gnasher Unleashed!
programme.desc: Pieface is secretly doing underpants laundry chores for Walter, hoping to help Dennis save up some cash. He urges the gang to audition for a replacement Pieface to make up for his mysterious absence.

programme.title: Danger Mouse
programme.desc: Danger Mouse's attempts to boost Penfold's confidence backfire when they lead to a ferocious games monster escaping into the real world.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: When Stinkweasel drops a rain of yukkiness onto the forest, the Fairy Squad, with their excellent flying skills, decide they are the ones for the job. However, Hoofius insists this should be their quest, even if he does hate ick! And when the Fairy Squad get their wings gunked and are unable to fly, the heroes can resume their quest to end Stinkweasel’s reign of stinky nonsense - no flying required.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: Herbert has invented a new contraption to help him fly using an old set of bagpipes. The 'Herbecopter', as Herbert likes to call it, is rather noisy but extremely effective, and Twinkle is unhappy at no longer being the only flying hero. So, when the heroes quest to get Friendlyface’s priceless locket back from a dragon, Twinkle and Herbert become extremely competitive and risk completely failing the quest.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings

programme.title: Duck and Frog

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Flop hear the familiar jingle of Gilly's ice cream van and race across the park to find her. After a long run, Bing finally gets his ice cream, but as he waves goodbye to Gilly he tips the ice cream out of the cone. It's too late to call Gilly back, so Flop makes a fruit cone out of the cone and some of his fruit kebab instead.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘sun’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. There are yellow, shining, setting, warm and sporty suns. We see Dee snowboard in the sun, and watch her and a friend help things grow in the sun! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Dad is taking Maddie to school on his bicycle, but their journey through the park soon turns into an intergalactic space adventure. They listen to the sounds around them and imagine themselves as brave explorers, shooting like rockets into the unknown.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri sings a sad song, which makes everyone cry – even herself.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button get creative with empty toilet rolls and turn into Froggie robots.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos visit a house where a parrot lives. The parrot is very noisy. The Twirlywoos enjoy copying the parrot's movements, which excites the parrot, causing it to squawk very loudly indeed. The table is making a noise and so is the Fruit Tea Machine, and when the doors join in too it becomes very noisy. The Hooter is noisier than everything though.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Educational series using Makaton sign language. Justin has lots of autumn fun with his friends, but Mr Tumble can't play football because leaves are blocking the goal.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: When the Tubby Phone rings, Dipsy comes slowly down on the Dup Dup to answer it - and then goes back up again! The Teletubbies all have fun doing the Dipsy Tubby Phone dance and watch a Tummy Tale about a boy travelling up in a lift that takes him into the treetops.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome little ones Araiya, Oakley, Tommy, Sullivan, Samaa and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Nigel has a book inside his bag. All the parents and babies have books with different words and pictures too, which are explored through play, songs and a story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to hide a baby-appropriate book inside a fabric bag or pillowcase to explore with their baby. Some viewers at home show how they’ve been reading books and sharing stories too. The nursery rhyme This Is the Way We Read a Book features, as does a story about Baby Bear’s favourite book. The Together Song gets everyone moving about before some calm time with sensory lights and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children play doctor with dolls, learning British Sign Language signs for doctor, sick and bed, then sing and sign Miss Polly Had a Dolly.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Aaron, Nelly and Adrian explore the wonderful world of plants that live in the shade, with some help from resident shady plant, Fearny the fern.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Twiggy the giraffe spends some time by herself. Hamza spots some incredible black rhinos in the wild and helps Ronald the vet give Thompson’s gazelle Ruka a check-up.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger is stuck in a tree, so the Pea-Rexes seek the tallest Vegesaurs to rescue her.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Playing butterflies in the backyard is great fun, until Bluey runs away with Judo, leaving Bingo all alone. Now poor Bingo is heartbroken, and Bluey needs to make amends.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: It's a scorcher of a day. Luckily, Duggee has a big paddling pool. Yippee! First of all, they need help with blowing up the pool and filling it with water. Thank goodness for Ethel the elephant, she can do everything. Time for the Squirrels to have lots of fun. Watch Tag, Betty, Norrie, Happy and Roly and all their animal friends have fun in the pool under the watchful eye of lifeguard Duggee.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Brown takes the Colourblocks exploring in the forest. Learn different ways to mix brown with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Henry wants to know all about brilliant beetles. Chantelle is with farm vet Claire, looking for some teeny tiny creatures who love to recycle. Meanwhile, Rory and his son Sandy are looking around the garden for little beetles and find a jumpy surprise. Chantelle and Rory’s fact files explain how big beetles are, whether they can fly and how beetles smell. It’s also time to find out how beetles recycle rubbish like animal poo. Sandy’s friend Zoe joins for this episode’s Teeny Tiny Task - making a beetle log pyramid.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Eden and Ava love pretending and make-believe. In this episode, they enjoy a pretend picnic in their bedroom and invent amazing recipes like strawberry stew and vegetable cake! They’re so yummy that Mum gets the hiccups. Later, Eden and Ava build a den for the whole family to hide in. They imagine they’re camping in the woods and look out at the stars. But will they be safe from the noisy tiger in the forest? Roar!

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: Jen brings a boat into the cafe and teaches Small about sailing. Meanwhile, Small finds out how aubergines grow. They use them to make Wayne the Whale a delicious plate of food.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Newfoundland Sylvie is a big therapy dog who loves to help people when they are worried with big soft cuddles. She and her owner Katrina visit all sorts of people every day, young and old. Sylvie and Katrina are helping a little boy called Alfie who is visiting his great-grandfather 'Pop-Pop' for the first time at the Woofton Care Home - and Alfie’s a bit nervous. Pop-Pop has just moved in, so the care home is a new place for everyone. And a new place needs a brave face. Sylvie has a feeling lots of people will be in need of her super heart!

programme.title: Time for School
programme.desc: It’s a new day, and Mrs Farrell is checking in with all the children to see how they are. Lucas tells her he is looking for more friends to play with, and there are lots of volunteers! Isla, Otto and Jud bake some delicious tiger ginger biscuits, using coloured icing for roar-some decorations. At playtime, Jud asks if she can play with Lucas, and they have a fun-filled game of chase. The day ends with carpet-time, and Lucas is happy with his new-found friends.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: AJ takes Evie and Anaya swimming, but Waffle must stay at home with Simon. Refusing to miss out on the fun, Waffle begins an adventure of his own and sets off to find Evie.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Isabelle is staying with Oona for the night, and Oona wants to impress her with something special. They leave the Puffin Burrows to take a midnight journey to see the most amazing sight - plankton lighting up the sea. Along the way, they are joined by Marvin and the Hoots. Oona can't wait to show her friends the beautiful sea lights!

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Barnaby is in the mood for hugs, but not all his friends are.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs build a fort in their garden, but their game is interrupted. Phillip keeps kicking his ball over the fence. Maddie finds it frustrating until she realises that Phillip wants more than just his ball back, but he just doesn't know how to ask.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Kitty wants to experience the way Sasha bounces everywhere. The Piggy Builders create an egg-shaped vehicle for Kitty. Wilf makes it go wild, and the Piggy Builders have to find a way to stop it!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: The number friends all want to do different things today, so rocket Ten finds a clever way to do them all. Learn all the ways to add to ten with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: O meets a wig and thinks it is the cutest pet he has ever seen. He is overjoyed to find out that it goes on his head, but then he wants it bigger. And bigger... This episode has fun with a host of letters and the words wig, dig, pig and big.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Educational series using Makaton sign language. Mr Tumble plays hide-and-seek, while Justin and his friends play inside and outside.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: When it rains it's no problem for the Teletubbies. They hurry inside Home Dome and eat tubby toast. Afterwards, they dance and splash in the puddles made by the rain... just like the children in Tummy Tales.

programme.title: Andy's Prehistoric Adventures
programme.desc: Preschool adventure series. Andy and his time-travelling clock head 160 million years into the past in search of a feather belonging to a tiny prehistoric dinosaur called the epidexipteryx. But an encounter with a hungry meat-eating dinosaur leaves Andy stranded in the tree tops.

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s Stall. She chooses the small instruction manual and remembers the day she got it. Bob is fixing Moira’s new vacuum cleaner, but unfortunately the instructions are in French and he can’t make sense of them. When Mrs Juniper arrives, Bob and Mack discover she has a hidden talent - she can speak French. Mack wonders if he has a hidden talent, and Bob reminds him he does - for sneaky sneaking. Mack remembers Bob has a talent for being a great ‘dada’ to his fluffy chicks. When Molly and James arrive at the Hub, they recall Alice’s gift for practical jokes. Then Moira stops by and they all cast their minds back to the time she showed off her flair for roller skating - even though she’d forgotten how to stop. By the time Bob fixes Moira’s vacuum cleaner, we find out that everyone in the Hub has a special hidden talent.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, CBeebies’ very own motorcycle rider, Grace, shows off three amazing racing machines. Grace drives an incredible racing powerboat, shows off a super-fast racing plane and takes a winged stock car for a spin.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: Miss Collie brings her pet stick insect, Woody, to class, but halfway through the day, Woody mysteriously vanishes! Dodge, Woofer, and Jazz spring into action, convinced a pup has taken him, and launch an investigation to track down the culprit. Just as Dodge thinks he’s cracked the case, they discover Woody was in his tank all along, showing off some surprising skills!

programme.desc: Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes must teach a lost baby Bokchoydactyl how to fly.

programme.desc: When Peter makes a rash promise to appease an angry Tommy Brock, he and his friends find themselves worming for their lives!

programme.desc: The Squirrels are looking for Duggee but can’t find him. Instead, they find someone they think is Enid, only much too big... Duggee has painted his face to look like Enid! Of course, the Squirrels want their faces painted too, so Duggee sets to it.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Zigzag hurts her foot on the job, Vida is there to help fix it. But Zigzag still has to deliver her packages in time for Vida's surprise Vet Day party.

programme.desc: Carrot wants to become superstrong, so she restores Evil Pea’s robot suit for herself.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: It's Evie and Doug's first playdate together with their friends. They try out their new ball pit, but Waffle can't join in because he's not toilet trained. He finds fun elsewhere.

programme.desc: Rafi makes gingerbread people for the bakery but thinks they look messy next to Jake’s neat ones. She wishes them to be perfect - and suddenly they spring to life! The cheeky gingerbreads dash through the café, splattering icing and riding on Deborah’s back as they try to reach Gingerbread Land. With Jake’s help, Rafi traps them under a cake dome. Dash reminds her that their messy look is what makes them special.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran go swimming in a lido on a hot summer day. JoJo is excited to show Gran Gran what she has learnt in her recent swimming lessons, but when she loses her goggles, she isn’t sure she can jump into the water. After spending more time in the pool with Gran Gran, JoJo learns to jump in without her goggles – making a big splash!

programme.desc: Baby Soup Dragon is upset because his mother won't let him use her big ladle and help make the soup. Tiny and Small tell him not to worry, he can help them instead. He does, and he enjoys it so much that he decides he wants to be a Clanger instead of a Soup Dragon. But after a little while, the Clangers are not so sure this is a good idea!

programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa discover a dandelion clock and have fun blowing the seeds. The Yummies show MeMo and BaBa how to plant dandelion seeds, and MeMo and BaBa marvel at how a seed can become a beautiful flower. They travel across the Lullaby Lake, making their way to the Bay of Books.

programme.desc: Igglepiggle and Upsy Daisy are best friends, but Igglepiggle can't find Upsy Daisy. He looks everywhere and asks everyone. He asks Makka Pakka. He asks the Tombliboos, until finally Upsy Daisy's bed leads him back to Upsy Daisy.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘sun’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. There are yellow, shining, setting, warm and sporty suns. We see Dee snowboard in the sun, and watch her and a friend help things grow in the sun! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Dad is taking Maddie to school on his bicycle, but their journey through the park soon turns into an intergalactic space adventure. They listen to the sounds around them and imagine themselves as brave explorers, shooting like rockets into the unknown.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri sings a sad song, which makes everyone cry – even herself.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button get creative with empty toilet rolls and turn into Froggie robots.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos visit a house where a parrot lives. The parrot is very noisy. The Twirlywoos enjoy copying the parrot's movements, which excites the parrot, causing it to squawk very loudly indeed. The table is making a noise and so is the Fruit Tea Machine, and when the doors join in too it becomes very noisy. The Hooter is noisier than everything though.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Educational series using Makaton sign language. Justin has lots of autumn fun with his friends, but Mr Tumble can't play football because leaves are blocking the goal.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: When the Tubby Phone rings, Dipsy comes slowly down on the Dup Dup to answer it - and then goes back up again! The Teletubbies all have fun doing the Dipsy Tubby Phone dance and watch a Tummy Tale about a boy travelling up in a lift that takes him into the treetops.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome little ones Araiya, Oakley, Tommy, Sullivan, Samaa and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Nigel has a book inside his bag. All the parents and babies have books with different words and pictures too, which are explored through play, songs and a story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to hide a baby-appropriate book inside a fabric bag or pillowcase to explore with their baby. Some viewers at home show how they’ve been reading books and sharing stories too. The nursery rhyme This Is the Way We Read a Book features, as does a story about Baby Bear’s favourite book. The Together Song gets everyone moving about before some calm time with sensory lights and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children play doctor with dolls, learning British Sign Language signs for doctor, sick and bed, then sing and sign Miss Polly Had a Dolly.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Aaron, Nelly and Adrian explore the wonderful world of plants that live in the shade, with some help from resident shady plant, Fearny the fern.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Twiggy the giraffe spends some time by herself. Hamza spots some incredible black rhinos in the wild and helps Ronald the vet give Thompson’s gazelle Ruka a check-up.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger is stuck in a tree, so the Pea-Rexes seek the tallest Vegesaurs to rescue her.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Playing butterflies in the backyard is great fun, until Bluey runs away with Judo, leaving Bingo all alone. Now poor Bingo is heartbroken, and Bluey needs to make amends.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: It's a scorcher of a day. Luckily, Duggee has a big paddling pool. Yippee! First of all, they need help with blowing up the pool and filling it with water. Thank goodness for Ethel the elephant, she can do everything. Time for the Squirrels to have lots of fun. Watch Tag, Betty, Norrie, Happy and Roly and all their animal friends have fun in the pool under the watchful eye of lifeguard Duggee.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Brown takes the Colourblocks exploring in the forest. Learn different ways to mix brown with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Henry wants to know all about brilliant beetles. Chantelle is with farm vet Claire, looking for some teeny tiny creatures who love to recycle. Meanwhile, Rory and his son Sandy are looking around the garden for little beetles and find a jumpy surprise. Chantelle and Rory’s fact files explain how big beetles are, whether they can fly and how beetles smell. It’s also time to find out how beetles recycle rubbish like animal poo. Sandy’s friend Zoe joins for this episode’s Teeny Tiny Task - making a beetle log pyramid.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Eden and Ava love pretending and make-believe. In this episode, they enjoy a pretend picnic in their bedroom and invent amazing recipes like strawberry stew and vegetable cake! They’re so yummy that Mum gets the hiccups. Later, Eden and Ava build a den for the whole family to hide in. They imagine they’re camping in the woods and look out at the stars. But will they be safe from the noisy tiger in the forest? Roar!

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: Jen brings a boat into the cafe and teaches Small about sailing. Meanwhile, Small finds out how aubergines grow. They use them to make Wayne the Whale a delicious plate of food.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Newfoundland Sylvie is a big therapy dog who loves to help people when they are worried with big soft cuddles. She and her owner Katrina visit all sorts of people every day, young and old. Sylvie and Katrina are helping a little boy called Alfie who is visiting his great-grandfather 'Pop-Pop' for the first time at the Woofton Care Home - and Alfie’s a bit nervous. Pop-Pop has just moved in, so the care home is a new place for everyone. And a new place needs a brave face. Sylvie has a feeling lots of people will be in need of her super heart!

programme.title: Time for School
programme.desc: It’s a new day, and Mrs Farrell is checking in with all the children to see how they are. Lucas tells her he is looking for more friends to play with, and there are lots of volunteers! Isla, Otto and Jud bake some delicious tiger ginger biscuits, using coloured icing for roar-some decorations. At playtime, Jud asks if she can play with Lucas, and they have a fun-filled game of chase. The day ends with carpet-time, and Lucas is happy with his new-found friends.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: AJ takes Evie and Anaya swimming, but Waffle must stay at home with Simon. Refusing to miss out on the fun, Waffle begins an adventure of his own and sets off to find Evie.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Isabelle is staying with Oona for the night, and Oona wants to impress her with something special. They leave the Puffin Burrows to take a midnight journey to see the most amazing sight - plankton lighting up the sea. Along the way, they are joined by Marvin and the Hoots. Oona can't wait to show her friends the beautiful sea lights!

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Barnaby is in the mood for hugs, but not all his friends are.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs build a fort in their garden, but their game is interrupted. Phillip keeps kicking his ball over the fence. Maddie finds it frustrating until she realises that Phillip wants more than just his ball back, but he just doesn't know how to ask.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Kitty wants to experience the way Sasha bounces everywhere. The Piggy Builders create an egg-shaped vehicle for Kitty. Wilf makes it go wild, and the Piggy Builders have to find a way to stop it!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: The number friends all want to do different things today, so rocket Ten finds a clever way to do them all. Learn all the ways to add to ten with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: O meets a wig and thinks it is the cutest pet he has ever seen. He is overjoyed to find out that it goes on his head, but then he wants it bigger. And bigger... This episode has fun with a host of letters and the words wig, dig, pig and big.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Educational series using Makaton sign language. Mr Tumble plays hide-and-seek, while Justin and his friends play inside and outside.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: When it rains it's no problem for the Teletubbies. They hurry inside Home Dome and eat tubby toast. Afterwards, they dance and splash in the puddles made by the rain... just like the children in Tummy Tales.

programme.title: Andy's Prehistoric Adventures
programme.desc: Preschool adventure series. Andy and his time-travelling clock head 160 million years into the past in search of a feather belonging to a tiny prehistoric dinosaur called the epidexipteryx. But an encounter with a hungry meat-eating dinosaur leaves Andy stranded in the tree tops.

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s Stall. She chooses the small instruction manual and remembers the day she got it. Bob is fixing Moira’s new vacuum cleaner, but unfortunately the instructions are in French and he can’t make sense of them. When Mrs Juniper arrives, Bob and Mack discover she has a hidden talent - she can speak French. Mack wonders if he has a hidden talent, and Bob reminds him he does - for sneaky sneaking. Mack remembers Bob has a talent for being a great ‘dada’ to his fluffy chicks. When Molly and James arrive at the Hub, they recall Alice’s gift for practical jokes. Then Moira stops by and they all cast their minds back to the time she showed off her flair for roller skating - even though she’d forgotten how to stop. By the time Bob fixes Moira’s vacuum cleaner, we find out that everyone in the Hub has a special hidden talent.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, CBeebies’ very own motorcycle rider, Grace, shows off three amazing racing machines. Grace drives an incredible racing powerboat, shows off a super-fast racing plane and takes a winged stock car for a spin.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: Miss Collie brings her pet stick insect, Woody, to class, but halfway through the day, Woody mysteriously vanishes! Dodge, Woofer, and Jazz spring into action, convinced a pup has taken him, and launch an investigation to track down the culprit. Just as Dodge thinks he’s cracked the case, they discover Woody was in his tank all along, showing off some surprising skills!

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes must teach a lost baby Bokchoydactyl how to fly.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: It’s an underwater mystery when a valuable protective shell goes missing.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter makes a rash promise to appease an angry Tommy Brock, he and his friends find themselves worming for their lives!

programme.title: Hey Duggee

programme.title: Vida the Vet

programme.title: Supertato

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Dad agrees to play sheepdog with Bluey and Bingo to stop them from disturbing Mum.

programme.title: Bluey

programme.title: G'wed
programme.desc: Ballroom legend Mary Mallan returns to Allsbrooke and reignites a decades-old rivalry with Grandma Pat. They settle it with a ballroom showdown, each training an unlikely partner - Pat pairs with a reluctant Christopher, while Mary trains Reece. As rehearsals grow brutal, Aimee and Mia-Louise turn the feud into a school craze with merch, rumours and betting. Beneath the rivalry, old wounds surface as Pat reveals abandoned dance dreams, a pregnancy that ended her career, and her belief Mary betrayed her. Christopher commits as he realises what the contest means to Pat, while Reece helps Mary confront life beyond trophies. On show night, both dances move the crowd before Pat and Christopher win. Backstage, Mary and Pat discover the betrayal never happened and finally heal.

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Eddie Kadi hosts the classic panel show with a twist where four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Chizzy Akudolu and Stephen K Amos to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this edition sees Nina Wadia, DJ Target, Josh Jones and Eddie Nestor join the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will do battle over four rounds - from guessing why those unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this series is about educating as much as entertaining with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

programme.title: Law & Order: UK
programme.desc: Crime drama series about the two vital parts of the criminal justice system - the police who investigate crime, and the Crown Prosecution Service who bring the offenders to trial. DS Ronnie Brooks is joined by his new partner DS Joe Hawkins as they investigate the death of jeweller Harry Bernstein, whose body is found minus his hands and teeth. The dead man's wife Lindsay, her lover David, and a former business associate of Harry's are all suspects, but the case then takes an unexpected turn when Harry's severed hands are delivered in a box to his sister Rebecca's house and accompanied by a short written message - 'Not Guilty'. Could this be because Rebecca is on the jury for the trial of Dale Horgan, a drug dealer and murderer whom Ronnie has been trying to nail for years? In court, Jacob Thorne and Kate Barker are faced with formidable defence barrister Eleanor Richmond, but will Ronnie's evidence be enough to convict?

programme.title: Trial & Retribution

Susan has been mutilated and sexually assaulted with an arrowhead weapon, and so a murder case is launched and an AMIP squad headed by Detective Superintendent Walker is called in to investigate - the only lead they have is witness Shiree Moyer, who saw Susan on the night she went missing talking to a man in a white van.
